strategy.description:
Startup strategy controlling how initialization failures are handled.

- `blocking`: Initialization runs before DNS resolution starts; errors are logged but Blocky keeps running if possible.
- `failOnError`: Like blocking but Blocky exits with an error if initialization fails.
- `fast`: Blocky serves DNS immediately and runs initialization in the background.

init.description: Initialization strategy controlling when upstream resolvers are tested on startup.

timeout.description: Timeout for upstream DNS connections; a value <= 0 is reset to the default.

groups.description: Named groups of upstream DNS resolvers; the "default" group is required.

strategy.description:
Strategy for selecting which upstream(s) to use per query (parallel_best, random, strict).

- `parallel_best`: Picks 2 random weighted resolvers per query and returns the fastest answer (default).
- `strict`: Queries upstreams in strict order; the next is tried only if the previous fails.
- `random`: Picks one random weighted resolver per query; another is tried on failure.
- `round_robin`: Rotates through upstreams in order, one per query.
- `weighted_round_robin`: Rotates through upstreams proportionally to their weight.
- `weighted_random`: Picks one upstream at random with probability proportional to its weight.
- `time_hop`: Sticks to one random upstream for a random interval, then hops to another.
- `domain_shard`: Hashes the query's eTLD+1 so the same domain always uses the same upstream.
- `recursive`: Resolves recursively from the root servers instead of forwarding.

userAgent.description: HTTP User-Agent header sent when connecting to DoH upstream servers.

maxIdleTimeout.description: Maximum idle duration before the QUIC connection is closed.

keepAlivePeriod.description: Interval at which keep-alive packets are sent to maintain the QUIC connection.

quic.description: QUIC-specific connection settings used when DoQ upstreams are configured.

strategy.description: Strategy for this group; zero/absent falls back to the global Upstreams.Strategy.

hopMin.description: Minimum duration to stick to one upstream when strategy is time_hop.

hopMax.description: Maximum duration to stick to one upstream when strategy is time_hop.

additionalProperties.description: UpstreamGroupConfig holds per-group settings overriding the global ones.

groupConfig.description: Per-group settings overriding the global strategy.

rotateHours.description:
Hours between shard-salt rotations. The domain->upstream mapping is stable
within a rotation window and moves across windows, so no single upstream
keeps a permanent stable slice of the user's domains. 0 disables rotation
(a permanent, fingerprintable mapping). Trade-off: rotation spreads a
domain's history across upstreams over time but loses upstream cache
locality at each window boundary.

domainShard.description: DomainShard holds settings for the domain_shard strategy.

upstreams.description: Upstream DNS servers and strategy configuration.

connectIPVersion.description:
IP version used for outgoing connections (dual, v4, v6).

- `dual`: Use both IPv4 and IPv6.
- `v4`: Use IPv4 only.
- `v6`: Use IPv6 only.

rewrite.description: Domain rewrite rules applied before resolution; keys are rewritten to their values.

fallbackUpstream.description: If true, the original query is sent upstream when the mapped resolver returns an empty answer.

customTTL.description: TTL for DNS records defined in the mapping section (does not apply to zone file records).

mapping.description: Simple domain-to-IP mappings; multiple IPs per domain separated by commas.

zone.description: DNS zone file content for more complex record definitions (A, AAAA, CNAME, TXT, SRV).

filterUnmappedTypes.description: If true, queries for types not defined for a domain return empty; if false, they are forwarded upstream.

nxdomain.description:
Domains answered with NXDOMAIN (name error) instead of a record. Exact match
only. Use for signals that require a real NXDOMAIN rather than a 0.0.0.0 block
— e.g. Firefox's use-application-dns.net canary, which disables DoH only on
NXDOMAIN. Matched before the zone/mapping.

target.description:
Directory for CSV log files, file path for sqlite, or database URL for mysql/postgresql/timescale,
or dnstap socket address (unix:/path, tcp://host:port, or bare /path for unix).

type.description:
Log target type: mysql, postgresql, timescale, sqlite, csv, csv-client, console, dnstap, or none.

- `console`: Log to console output (used when no type is set).
- `none`: Do not log any queries.
- `mysql`: Log each query to an external MySQL or MariaDB database.
- `postgresql`: Log each query to an external PostgreSQL database.
- `csv`: Log to a CSV file (one per day).
- `csv-client`: Log to a CSV file (one per day and per client).
- `timescale`: Log each query to an external Timescale database.
- `sqlite`: Log each query to a local SQLite database file.
- `dnstap`: Export query/response events via dnstap (Frame Streams).

rfc6762-appendixG.description:
These are "recommended for private use" but not mandatory.
If a user wishes to use one, it will most likely be via conditional
upstream or custom DNS, which come before SUDN in the resolver chain.
Thus defaulting to `true` and returning NXDOMAIN here should not conflict.

enable.description: Set to false to completely disable Special Use Domain Name blocking (not recommended for remote upstreams).

specialUseDomains.description: Special Use Domain Names (SUDN) blocking configuration.

enable.description: Enable DNS64 synthesis of AAAA records from A records for IPv6-only clients (RFC 6147).

prefixes.description: IPv6 prefixes used for synthesis; valid lengths are /32, /40, /48, /56, /64, /96 (default: 64:ff9b::/96).

exclusionSet.description: IPv6 prefixes excluded from triggering synthesis. Overrides the default exclusion set; advanced use only.

trustAnchors.description: Custom trust anchors (DNSKEY or DS records); empty uses built-in IANA root trust anchors.

maxChainDepth.description: Maximum domain label depth for chain of trust validation (DoS protection).

cacheExpirationHours.description: How long to cache DNSSEC validation results, in hours.

maxUpstreamQueries.description: DoS protection: max upstream queries per validation

clockSkewToleranceSec.description:
Clock skew tolerance in seconds for signature validation (default: 3600 = 1 hour)
Allows validation to succeed even if system clock is off by this amount.
Matches Unbound/BIND defaults for real-world deployments (VMs, containers, embedded systems).
Per RFC 6781 §4.1.2: Validators should account for clock skew in deployment environments.

ipv6Prefix.description: Prefix length used to aggregate IPv6 client addresses into a single bucket.

allowlist.description: CIDRs or IPs that are never rate-limited.

rateLimit.description: Per-client DNS query rate limiting configuration.

enable.description: Enable DNS rebinding protection for answers from the general upstream resolvers.

allowedDomains.description: Domains (including their subdomains) that may resolve to non-public IPs (split-horizon DNS).

replayWeight.description:
Source-weighted noise repartition (pick source by weight, then a domain
within it — the list's ~1.8M count never affects source odds). Large spread
so the user's own domains dominate: replay+corpus (visited) : list ≈ 20:1.
Companions are a separate, higher tier — triggered per real query
(companionPct), so realistic page-load bursts dominate the noise overall.

listWeight.description: Tranco 1M public static list (thin breadth layer)

activeHoursStart.description: 0-23; full rate within [start,end), floor rate outside

refreshURL.description: optional live list source; empty = embedded

diurnalShaping.description: Obfuscation techniques (all default-on; each independently toggleable).

replayMutate.description: mutate replayed queries so they aren't byte-identical

fingerprintMatch.description: stamp EDNS shape sampled from real clients

splitUpstream.description: vary decoy client identity to diverge group routing

missChaffPct.description: % of decoys that are likely-NXDOMAIN random labels

clusterPct.description: % of timer emissions that fire a small related burst (secondary to CompanionPct)

reactiveVolume.description: Reactive obfuscation: track live real traffic instead of the 7-day historical shape.

companionPct.description: % of real queries that trigger a browse-style companion cluster derived from that domain

cohortPct.description:
Structural emission (7G/#1/#5): shape the SEQUENCE and TEXTURE of decoy
emissions after real browsing instead of IID picks.

sessionCoherence.description: walk plausible session chains (NextInSession/SessionSeed) instead of IID domain picks

stepPct.description: within a session, % chance to advance to a topically-plausible successor vs. reseeding a fresh session

revisitCadence.description: re-emit corpus/replay domains on their learned revisit interval (jittered) instead of flat random

cohortJitterMs.description:
Cohort-replay perturbation: keep the recorded texture but break the exact
1:1 echo — jitter each sub-resource offset (the re-sort turns overlapping
jitter into small run-to-run reordering) and splice in a small % companion.

cohortCompanionPct.description: % of cohort replays that splice in one unrelated companion at a random point in the load

personaCover.description:
Compensating persona cover (#8): TOTAL egress tracks a household diurnal
target curve, so decoy_rate(t) = max(0, targetCurve(t) − recentRealQPM).
This hides the activity LEVEL (not just which queries are real) without
delaying real queries — the box always looks like a generic household on
the wire. When off, the engine falls back to the reactive/diurnal path.

Residual: real usage ABOVE the peak ceiling still spikes total egress — the
curve hides level only up to targetQpmPeak, by design (a truly constant
max-rate cover would cost fixed bandwidth we don't pay on a home box).

personaProfile.description:
PersonaProfile selects the persona-curve preset the compensating cover aims
for: "home" (peak/trough 40/6), "enterprise" (300/60, office-diurnal over a
24/7 IoT floor), or "auto" (home baseline; the engine may escalate toward the
enterprise curve from observed client classes). The explicit TargetQPM* fields
still override the preset (see EffectivePersonaCurve). "auto" is the default so
a home box behaves exactly as before this field existed.

targetQpmPeak.description: busy-hour target total egress (queries/min); the shipped home default

targetQpmTrough.description: pre-dawn quiet target total egress (queries/min); the shipped home default

enable.description:
Enable turns on classification + per-class shaping. Off = every client gets
the browsing-shaped cover (pre-device-class behaviour).

vendorTelemetry.description:
VendorTelemetry emits vendor-telemetry chaff (fixed beacon endpoints) for
iot/server-classed clients instead of browse companions.

vendorFamilies.description:
VendorFamilies names which telemetry families to draw beacon domains from
(e.g. "apple", "google", "amazon", "microsoft", "samsung", "tuya", "sonos").
Empty = the engine's built-in default family set.

phantomDevicesPct.description:
PhantomDevicesPct is the share of vendor-telemetry chaff drawn from families
NOT present in the real fleet, to obscure true fleet size and vendor mix.
0 = only mirror observed vendors.

deviceClass.description:
Device-class awareness: classify each client from its real DNS behavior
(iot / workstation / server / unknown) and shape its cover accordingly.

chatterPct.description:
Per-query realism + operational (device chatter, transport/qtype/failure
diversity, per-client personas, adaptive back-off).

tcpPct.description: % of decoys stamped as TCP transport (req.Protocol); see engine limitation — blocky→upstream transport is upstream-config-global, not per-query

failChaffPct.description: % of emissions that deliberately query a likely-NXDOMAIN name so decoys don't always succeed

personaAttribution.description: attribute decoys to sampled real clients (stamp their ClientIP + fingerprint) so each client's on-wire profile stays consistent under noise

adaptiveBackoff.description: reduce the decoy rate when the recent decoy resolve error rate spikes (upstream strain / rate-limiting) and recover slowly

dualStackPct.description: % of A/AAAA decoys that also emit the sibling record (browser dual-stack)

offHoursFloorQPM.description: always-on Poisson floor rate outside active hours (never gate fully to zero)

activeHoursEdgeJitterMin.description: ± minutes of per-day jitter on the active-hours window edges

prewarmEnable.description:
Corpus pre-warming: proactively pull TRENDING/RISING domains into the noise
corpus before the user first visits them, so a genuinely new domain is
already covered by chaff. Offline-first: with no PrewarmURL it mines the
embedded Tranco list's mid-popularity band (ranks ~1k-50k, the domains a
normal person is likely to newly encounter), rotating the slab each run.

prewarmURL.description: optional trending source (Tranco rising / CF Radar CSV/txt); empty = embedded band

queryCaseRandomization.description:
QueryCaseRandomization applies DNS 0x20 case randomization (draft-vixie-dnsext-dns0x20)
to outgoing forwarded queries: each ASCII letter of the question name is independently
upper/lower-cased on the wire, the upstream must echo the exact case (spoofing defense),
and the answer is normalized back to the client's case. Forwarding path only; the
recursive (zdns) path ignores it until the documented zdns fork lands.

profiling.description:
Profiling is the opt-in, default-OFF presence/sleep/work analysis. Local-only,
never exported. See ProfilingConfig.

shadowBlockedQueries.description:
ShadowBlockedQueries decouples the client answer from the wire query for blocked
domains: the client still gets the block response (ad-blocking intact), but the
real upstream query is also egressed asynchronously and its answer discarded, so
real page-load cohorts stay complete on the wire and dissolve the "blocking
resolver" signature. Default ON, but it only ACTIVATES when the decoy engine is
also enabled (privacy.decoy.enable) — that is what gives the egressed tracker
queries their decoy cover. Without the noise engine it stays inert, so a
blocking-only setup never egresses blocked-domain queries uncovered.

privacy.description: Privacy/decoy features: background noise queries, TTL jitter, EDNS padding.

enable.description:
Enable the background updater. Seeding from embedded assets still happens
on startup regardless, so downstream consumers always have data.

intervalHours.description: IntervalHours between upstream version checks (default weekly).

trancoUrl.description:
TrancoURL is the Tranco "latest list" API base. The updater GETs
<TrancoURL>/api/lists/date/latest for the list id, then downloads
<TrancoURL>/download/<id>/1000000.

blocklistRepo.description:
BlocklistRepo is the blocklistproject GitHub repo (owner/name) whose main
commit SHA gates blocklist refresh.

lists.description: Unified list-updater subsystem (Tranco decoy list + blocklistproject lists).
